sentences.en: emperor by staging these displays is kind of putting his reputation on the line.

sentences.en: So why does this mark a change in the Roman attitude towards gladiatorial games and the stadia in which they stage them?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这标志着罗马人对角斗比赛以及举办比赛的体育场馆的态度发生了转变？

sentences.en: But there is also a very obvious need to stamp their power, their authority, the existence of their dynasty on the urban fabric of the city.

sentences.en: And they're given the opportunity to do that by what Nero, the last of the Julia Claudian emperors, had done in a similar light.

sentences.en: So Nero had been emperor during the Great Fire.

sentences.en: We did an episode on him.

sentences.en: And in the wake of the Great Fire, he clears away all the rubble and builds this kind of enormous pleasure palace that features a house sheathed with gold so it glints in the sun.

sentences.en: He's got plans for an enormous colossus, giant statue with his own face, and a lake with pleasure gardens all around it.

sentences.en: And this is cast by the senatorial elite as being an absolute display of self-indulgence, which it clearly is.

sentences.en: People can just wander in willy-nilly.

sentences.zh: 我们是新王朝。

sentences.en: We can afford this, and we are giving it to you, the Roman people.
sentences.zh: 我们负担得起，我们把它送给你们，罗马人民。

sentences.en: And so that's why it's built on the massive scale that it is.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它被建成如此巨大的规模。

sentences.en: It's not just about fitting people in.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了容纳更多人。

sentences.en: It's about making a very, very visible statement.
sentences.zh: 这是为了发表一个非常、非常明显的声明。

sentences.en: So Catherine Welch, who's written a brilliant book on the evolution of the amphitheater from its beginnings up to the Colosseum,
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·韦尔奇写过一本关于圆形竞技场从起源到斗兽场演变的精彩著作，

sentences.en: has said about the Colosseum that it towered over the Roman cityscape in much the way that cathedrals later towered over medieval towns.
sentences.zh: 她曾说斗兽场在罗马城市景观中高耸入云，就像后来的大教堂在欧洲中世纪城镇中高耸入云一样。

sentences.en: And just cathedrals tell you a lot about the value systems of people in the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 正如大教堂能让你了解中世纪人们的价值体系一样。

sentences.en: So the fact that you have this great monument to sport and spectacle and blood sports tells you a lot about the value system of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这座伟大的体育、奇观和血腥运动的纪念碑，也让你了解了罗马人的价值体系。

sentences.en: And the extravagance of it is the point.
sentences.zh: 它的奢华本身就是重点。

sentences.en: And it's a pretty radical new design.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个非常激进的新设计。

sentences.en: So the outside, it has kind of huge statues.
sentences.zh: 外部有巨大的雕像。

sentences.en: It has different kinds of pillars and all kinds of things like that.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的柱子和类似的东西。

sentences.en: It has beautiful awnings.
sentences.zh: 有漂亮的遮阳篷。

sentences.en: It is designed to be spectacular.
sentences.zh: 它的设计旨在引人注目。

sentences.en: And the further benefit of this for the Flavians is that it enables them to remind people who are going there about the great military triumph of the Flavian dynasty,
sentences.zh: 对于弗拉维王朝来说，这还有一个额外的好处，那就是它能提醒去那里的人们记住弗拉维王朝伟大的军事胜利，

sentences.en: which is the defeat of the Judeans, and specifically Titus' capture of Jerusalem, which has been stripped of its treasures,
sentences.zh: 即对犹太人的征服，特别是提图斯对耶路撒冷的占领，耶路撒冷被剥夺了财宝，

sentences.en: and these treasures have been paraded through the streets of Rome.
sentences.zh: 这些财宝在罗马街头游行展示。

sentences.en: Now, this is a slight of hand, because actually there wasn't much treasure in Judea.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种障眼法，因为实际上犹太并没有多少财宝。

sentences.en: The Flavians are massively exaggerating how much loot they have taken.
sentences.zh: 弗拉维王朝大大夸大了他们掠夺的战利品数量。

sentences.en: In fact, the money seems to have come from Vespasian and Titus hugely raising taxes on the eastern half of the empire.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些钱似乎来自韦斯巴芗和提图斯对帝国东部地区大幅加税。

sentences.en: But it's all good stuff.
sentences.zh: 但这都是好事。

sentences.en: A Roman emperor, the word emperor comes from imperator, which literally means general.
sentences.zh: 罗马皇帝，皇帝（emperor）这个词来自imperator，字面意思是将军。

sentences.en: So it's Vespasian and Titus saying, we are imperatoris.
sentences.zh: 所以这是韦斯巴芗和提图斯在说，我们是统帅（imperatoris）。

sentences.en: We are an imperator in the original sense of the word, not as Nero was, a man who never led an army, who just sat around playing the liar.
sentences.zh: 我们是原始意义上的统帅，不像尼禄，他从未带过兵，只是坐着弹竖琴。

sentences.en: So it's making a statement about the manliness of the Flavians and the manliness of the Roman people.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在宣扬弗拉维王朝的阳刚之气和罗马人民的阳刚之气。

sentences.en: And just on the Colosseum, the construction of it, we presumably have no idea who designed it, who built it.
sentences.zh: 关于斗兽场的建造，我们大概不知道是谁设计的，是谁建造的。

sentences.en: These things are lost to us, are they?
sentences.zh: 这些信息都已经失传了，是吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I mean, it's often said that it's Judean slaves.
sentences.zh: 人们常说那是犹太奴隶干的。

sentences.en: It may well have been.
sentences.zh: 很可能确实如此。

sentences.en: A huge harvest of slaves was taken from Judea, and they would have provided a ready source of manpower.
sentences.zh: 从犹太地区掠夺了大量的奴隶，他们提供了现成的劳动力来源。

sentences.en: We know that Vespasian sends a whole troop of Judean slaves to Nero when he's trying to build his canal through the Isthmus of Corinth,
sentences.zh: 我们知道韦斯巴芗在尼禄试图修建科林斯地峡运河时，曾派出一整队犹太奴隶，

sentences.en: which never gets completed because Nero dies.
sentences.zh: 但因为尼禄去世，工程从未完成。

sentences.en: I think it's pretty clear that Judea is being used as a source of manpower for kind of big infrastructure projects.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，犹太地区被用作大型基础设施项目的劳动力来源。

sentences.en: And a capacity.
sentences.zh: 还有容量问题。

sentences.en: So I've seen different estimates from 50,000 to about 80,000 people.
sentences.zh: 我见过不同的估计，从5万人到8万人不等。

sentences.en: I mean, extraordinary when you consider the small size of the population compared with today that they are building a stadium of that size.
sentences.zh: 考虑到与今天相比人口规模较小，他们能建造如此规模的体育场，真是非同寻常。

sentences.en: But I suppose there's still an element of confusion in that, is it not set seats for everybody?
sentences.zh: 但我认为这里面还是有困惑的成分，难道不是每个人都有固定的座位吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the capacity can change depending on how many people you're choosing to pack in.
sentences.zh: 容量可能会根据你选择挤进多少人而改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this now comes to the specific question of why it matters to Titus.
sentences.zh: 现在这就引出了为什么这对提图斯很重要的具体问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So it's probable that the Colosseum is inaugurated by Titus in the summer of AD 80.
sentences.zh: 斗兽场很可能是在公元80年夏天由提图斯揭幕的。

sentences.en: It might have been 81, but more likely to be 80.
sentences.zh: 可能是81年，但更有可能是80年。

sentences.en: And that is a year after the subject of our previous podcast, the destruction of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
sentences.zh: 那是在我们上一期播客的主题——庞贝和赫库兰尼姆毁灭之后的一年。

sentences.en: And that is one of a number of disasters that rocks the reign of Titus.
sentences.zh: 那是震撼提图斯统治的一系列灾难之一。

sentences.en: So other disasters include a major outbreak of fire that destroys the Pantheon.
sentences.zh: 其他灾难还包括一场摧毁了万神殿的大火。

sentences.en: So this is why the Pantheon, the temple to all the gods will get rebuilt by Hadrian, the great dome building that most tourists to Rome will have seen,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么万神殿，这座供奉所有神灵的庙宇，会被哈德良皇帝重建，那座大多数去罗马的游客都见过的宏伟穹顶建筑，

sentences.en: the best preserved Roman temple.
sentences.zh: 它是保存最完好的罗马神庙。

sentences.en: But it also destroys the temple of Jupiter on the Capitol, which is the most significant sacred space in Rome.
sentences.zh: 但这也摧毁了卡比托利欧山上的朱庇特神庙，那是罗马最重要的神圣空间。

sentences.en: And it had already burnt down in the year of the four emperors when Vespasian comes to power, AD 69.
sentences.zh: 在公元69年，也就是维斯帕先掌权的“四帝之年”，它就已经被烧毁了。

sentences.en: And that had absolutely been taken as a terrifying symbol of the wrath of the gods, that that temple had been burnt down.
sentences.zh: 当时，那座神庙被烧毁，绝对被视为神灵愤怒的可怕征兆。

sentences.en: So the fact that Vespasian and Titus have been busy repairing it and now it's burnt down again, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以，维斯帕先和提图斯一直忙于修复它，而现在它又被烧毁了，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Then there's an awful plague that ravages Rome.
sentences.zh: 接着，一场可怕的瘟疫席卷了罗马。

sentences.en: Again, terrible.
sentences.zh: 同样，非常可怕。

sentences.en: And then of course you have the eruption of Vesuvius and the cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum were literally entombed.
sentences.zh: 当然，随后就是维苏威火山爆发，庞贝和赫库兰尼姆这两座城市简直是被活埋了。

sentences.en: So there are huge numbers of people who have not been given the funerary rites that they should have been.
sentences.zh: 因此，有大量的人没有得到他们本应得到的葬礼仪式。

sentences.en: And so the anxiety is that their restless ghosts are going to roam the world unappeased.
sentences.zh: 所以人们担心，他们不安的灵魂会在世间游荡，无法得到安息。

sentences.en: And so Titus has a desperate need to appease the spirits of these unburied dead.
sentences.zh: 因此，提图斯迫切需要安抚这些未被埋葬的死者的灵魂。

sentences.en: And I think there is no question when he inaugurates the Colosseum, he is trying to do it, not just as a kind of grand master of ceremonies,
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，当他为斗兽场揭幕时，他不仅是作为一名盛大的仪式主持者，

sentences.en: a man who is offering entertainment to the people, but as someone who is the moral guardian of the empire and of the city.
sentences.zh: 一个为民众提供娱乐的人，而是作为帝国和城市的道德守护者在行事。

sentences.en: So Titus had actually had quite a bad reputation before he becomes emperor.
sentences.zh: 事实上，提图斯在成为皇帝之前名声相当糟糕。

sentences.en: He'd been head of the Praetorians, so the kind of the imperial bodyguard, and that had given him quite a bad reputation.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任禁卫军首领，也就是帝国卫队的指挥官，这让他名声不佳。

sentences.en: He'd been a notorious libertine.
sentences.zh: 他曾是个臭名昭著的浪荡子。

sentences.en: So his most famous in Amarata was a Jewish princess called Berenice.
sentences.zh: 他最著名的情人是一位名叫贝勒尼基的犹太公主。

sentences.en: Oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗。

sentences.en: But when he becomes emperor, it's kind of like Prince Hal in Henry IV, part two, he turns over a new leaf and says, basically, I am going to be good.
sentences.zh: 但当他成为皇帝后，就像《亨利四世》第二部里的哈尔王子一样，他洗心革面，基本上说，我要做一个好人。

sentences.en: So when he accepts the office of Pontifex Maximus, which is the chief priesthood in the Roman state, he declares that he is motivated by one thing and one thing only,
sentences.zh: 所以，当他接受罗马国家最高祭司这一职位时，他宣称自己只受一个动机驱使，且仅此一个，

sentences.en: which is he never wants to pollute his hands with blood.
sentences.zh: 那就是他永远不想让自己的双手沾满鲜血。

sentences.en: That's very un-Roman, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这很不“罗马”。

sentences.en: Well, except that it's very ostentatious, and to be ostentatious in your programs is very Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了它非常显眼这一点，而在你的计划中追求显眼是非常“罗马”的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he has a habit of lying around at dinner, and he'll say things like, oh, my friends, I have wasted a day, for I have done nothing good.
sentences.zh: 他有一种在晚餐时躺着的习惯，他会说些诸如“哦，我的朋友们，我浪费了一天，因为我没做任何好事”之类的话。

sentences.en: I'm like that.
sentences.zh: 我就像那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道。

sentences.en: I know you are.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是。

sentences.en: So very, very Titus behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常、非常“提图斯”。

sentences.en: And so he's kind of widely reported as saying things like this.
sentences.zh: 所以他被广泛报道说出这样的话。

sentences.en: It obviously comes from his own propagandists.
sentences.zh: 这显然来自他自己的宣传人员。

sentences.en: And when he inaugurates the Colosseum, people whom he had employed as the head of the Praetorians, kind of informers,
sentences.zh: 当他为斗兽场揭幕时，那些他曾雇佣为禁卫军首领的人，也就是某种告密者，

sentences.en: the apparatus of spy craft that had been serving to uphold the Flavian regime, all these people are dragged into the arena.
sentences.zh: 那些一直服务于维护弗拉维王朝的间谍机构的人，所有这些人被拖进了竞技场。

sentences.en: They are smashed up with cudgels.
sentences.zh: 他们被棍棒殴打。

sentences.en: They are lashed with whips.
sentences.zh: 他们被鞭子抽打。

sentences.en: And this is, again, making an absolutely public statement to the mass of the Roman people that Titus is no longer the man he was,
sentences.zh: 这再次向广大罗马民众发表了一个绝对公开的声明：提图斯已不再是以前的那个他了，

sentences.en: that this is all about doing right by the Roman people, but more importantly, doing right by the gods.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了对罗马人民尽责，但更重要的是，对神灵尽责。

sentences.en: And it's because of that, that what you were fixing on, the seating aspect, is so important.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，你刚才提到的座位安排问题才如此重要。

sentences.en: Because a city in chaos is a city that is going to anger the gods.
sentences.zh: 因为一个陷入混乱的城市，是一个会激怒神灵的城市。

sentences.en: So Titus is, as Augustus was, obsessed with everyone having the right place.
sentences.zh: 所以提图斯和奥古斯都一样，执着于每个人都有合适的位置。

sentences.en: Senators have to be in the right place.
sentences.zh: 元老们必须在合适的位置。

sentences.en: The poor have to be right at the top, women, slaves, whatever.
sentences.zh: 穷人必须在最顶层，还有妇女、奴隶等等。

sentences.en: They all have to be.
sentences.zh: 他们都必须各就各位。

sentences.en: It's a census that is now embodied in the stone.
sentences.zh: 这是一种现在体现在石头上的普查。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's the seating.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是座位安排。

sentences.en: What are people watching?
sentences.zh: 人们在看什么？

sentences.en: So my sense of it, Tom, as a complete outsider to the subject and someone who loves the film Gladiator is that you've got a few men in chariots.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，作为这个主题的完全外行，也是电影《角斗士》的影迷，我的感觉是，你会看到几个驾着战车的人。

sentences.en: You've got a bloke with a net and a trident.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一个拿着网和三叉戟的家伙。

sentences.en: You've got the other fellow with his sword.
sentences.zh: 你会看到另一个拿着剑的家伙。

sentences.en: You've got a few tigers or whatever roaming around underneath and then suddenly being disgorged out of kind of grills.
sentences.zh: 你会看到几只老虎或什么东西在下面游荡，然后突然从某种格栅里被放出来。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 什么都有。

sentences.en: I mean, it is stupefying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这令人目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: These are the greatest spectacles ever staged.
sentences.zh: 这些是有史以来上演的最伟大的奇观。

sentences.en: And I think that what Titus is doing, again, it's kind of a repudiation of Nero and it's an affirmation of the fact that the Roman people have to align themselves with the gods.
sentences.zh: 我认为提图斯所做的，再次重申，是对尼禄的一种否定，也是对罗马人民必须与神灵保持一致这一事实的肯定。

sentences.en: So what Nero had done when he took to the stage and played on the lyre or took a dramatic role was that he was identifying himself with the heroes of myth.
sentences.zh: 尼禄登上舞台弹奏里拉琴或扮演戏剧角色时，他是在将自己与神话英雄等同起来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What Titus is doing is often kind of basically restaging the dimension of myth in the arena.
sentences.zh: 而提图斯所做的，基本上是在竞技场中重现神话的维度。

sentences.en: And that in turn is to cast him and the Roman people in the role in the part of the gods.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又将他和罗马人民置于神灵的角色中。

sentences.en: It's actually, people do this thing that they could live action role playing or cosplaying or whatever they call it, where they dress up as, yeah,
sentences.zh: 实际上，人们现在做的这种真人角色扮演或Cosplay，或者随便他们怎么称呼，他们打扮成，是的，

sentences.en: they dress up as people from the Viking heroes, characters in Star Wars, and they do what they do in woods or wherever they do it.
sentences.zh: 他们打扮成维京英雄、星球大战里的角色，然后在树林里或任何他们去的地方做他们做的事。

sentences.en: But this is a kind of version of that.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种那种行为的版本。

sentences.en: So it's a version of role playing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种角色扮演的版本。

sentences.en: They would dress up as heroes, as characters from history.
sentences.zh: 他们会打扮成英雄，打扮成历史人物。

sentences.en: So if the Roman people are the gods watching the spectacle of mortals on the earth,
sentences.zh: 如果罗马人民是观看地球上凡人奇观的神灵，

sentences.en: then the criminals and the slaves who are entertaining them are often being cast in the role of kind of tragic heroes, heroes from myth and so on.
sentences.zh: 那么娱乐他们的罪犯和奴隶往往被塑造成悲剧英雄、神话英雄等等的角色。

sentences.en: So there isn't a kind of set routine, but the whole point with staging spectacular is that you kind of mix things up.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有一套固定的程序，但上演奇观的全部意义在于你要把事情混合起来。

sentences.en: But you could say that there's a kind of a rhythm that is more obeyed than disregarded, which is that you open with displays of execution.
sentences.zh: 但你可以说有一种节奏，与其说是被打破，不如说是被遵循，那就是以处决表演开场。

sentences.en: And again, these are seen by the Romans as being an expression of the correct way to do things.
sentences.zh: 而且，罗马人再次将这些视为正确行事方式的一种表达。

sentences.en: So Livy says of the Romans that we may boast above any other people that our methods of punishment are civilized,
sentences.zh: 所以李维谈到罗马人时说，我们可以比任何其他民族更自豪的是，我们的惩罚方式是文明的，

sentences.en: which kind of may come as a surprise to us because we tend to think that Roman punishments are incredibly uncivilized.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我们感到惊讶，因为我们倾向于认为罗马的惩罚极其不文明。

sentences.en: But it is important to the Romans that executions affirm a moral order.
sentences.zh: 但对罗马人来说，重要的是处决要维护一种道德秩序。

sentences.en: What is happening in the Colosseum is that this kind of ambition to make executions affirm a kind of sense that all is right with the world is being fused with the dimension of myth.
sentences.zh: 在斗兽场里发生的事情是，这种让处决维护世界一切正常的雄心，正在与神话的维度相融合。

sentences.en: So in effect, what they're staging, it's a kind of combination of a snuff movie with Cirque du Soleil.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，他们上演的是一种“虐杀电影”与“太阳马戏团”的结合体。

sentences.en: It's capital punishment fused with brilliant stagecraft.
sentences.zh: 这是与精湛舞台艺术融合的死刑。

sentences.en: And I suppose it's the stagecraft and the spectacle that lifts it to the level of a ritual rather than merely, oh, here's some guy who stole some bread.
sentences.zh: 我想正是这种舞台艺术和奇观，将其提升到了仪式的层面，而不仅仅是“哦，这里有个偷面包的家伙，我们砍掉他的手或头”。

sentences.en: We'll cut his hands off or cut his head off.
sentences.zh: 我们砍掉他的手或头。

sentences.en: It's both.
sentences.zh: 两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I mean, again, it's having cake and eating it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这又是“鱼与熊掌兼得”。

sentences.en: And so Marshall loves these.
sentences.zh: 所以马提雅尔很喜欢这些。

sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So obviously it threatens.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这是一种威胁。

sentences.en: Yes, it's...
sentences.zh: 是的，它是……

sentences.en: Well, you know, if you go there, you are taking part in a ritual that is designed to appease the dead.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，如果你去那里，你就是在参与一种旨在安抚死者的仪式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's not very Christian.
sentences.zh: 那可不太像基督徒的行为。

sentences.en: So on the Coliseum, the Coliseum falls into a relative disuse, I guess, after the 5th century when Rome itself is on its uppers, the city.
sentences.zh: 关于斗兽场，我想在5世纪之后，当罗马城本身衰落时，它就相对荒废了。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Later on, as you said, it becomes a castle, the castle of the Francopans.
sentences.zh: 后来，正如你所说，它变成了一座城堡，弗兰吉帕尼家族的城堡。

sentences.en: The Francopans.
sentences.zh: 弗兰吉帕尼家族。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But before that, it's a chapel at one point.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，它一度是个小教堂。

sentences.en: And that's obviously because people think this was the place where Christians were martyred.
sentences.zh: 这显然是因为人们认为这里是基督徒殉道的地方。

sentences.en: Not sure.
sentences.zh: 不确定。

sentences.en: I think the idea that Christians were martyred is much later.
sentences.zh: 我认为基督徒在这里殉道的说法要晚得多。

sentences.en: I think it's the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是18世纪的事了。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: Yes, I think it's the 18th century that that happens.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为那是18世纪才出现的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think the Coliseum is always seen as the emblem of Rome because it's the fastest monument there.
sentences.zh: 但我认为斗兽场一直被视为罗马的象征，因为它是那里最宏伟的纪念碑。

sentences.en: You know, that idea that it is the Roman equivalent of a cathedral.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种认为它是罗马版大教堂的观点。

sentences.en: It's that kind of great statement in stone of what the city is.
sentences.zh: 它是这座城市在石头上留下的伟大宣言。

sentences.en: And the sheer size of it means it doesn't collapse when other buildings do.
sentences.zh: 它巨大的体积意味着当其他建筑倒塌时，它依然屹立不倒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, you know, even though it's in ruins now, it's still an extraordinary spectacle, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，即使它现在已成废墟，它仍然是一个非凡的奇观，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's a huge quarry, but it's so enormous that even though, you know, chunks of the stone gets carted away,
sentences.zh: 我是说，它是一个巨大的采石场，但它太庞大了，以至于尽管石块被运走，

sentences.en: it retains the form that it always had right the way up to the present day.
sentences.zh: 它依然保留着它自古以来一直保持的形态，直到今天。

sentences.en: And although, you know, we've made a lot of analogies with football and obviously the football, a lot of football stadiums do look like the Coliseum, actually,
sentences.zh: 虽然我们做了很多与足球的类比，而且显然很多足球场看起来确实像斗兽场，

sentences.en: if they're a sort of bowl shape, maybe a better analogy is actually the bullfighting arena.
sentences.zh: 如果它们是碗状的话，也许更好的类比其实是斗牛场。

sentences.en: Because bullfighting, there was talk at one point in the Coliseum's history, I think, about turning in the early modern period, turning it into a bullfighting arena.
sentences.zh: 因为在斗兽场的历史上，我想在近代早期，确实有人谈论过把它变成一个斗牛场。

sentences.en: It never happened.
sentences.zh: 但这从未实现。

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the popes, I think, wanted to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想其中一位教皇想这样做。

sentences.en: The popes.
sentences.zh: 教皇们。

sentences.en: And, you know, he was, you know, not an infallibly good idea.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不是一个绝对正确的主意。

sentences.en: So that was kind of a bush.
sentences.zh: 所以那只是个想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, so bullfighting, I think, is the closest that you would get to what the experience of gladiatorial combat would be.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我觉得斗牛场是最接近角斗比赛体验的地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, for aficionados of bullfighting, it's not just about the violence, not even perhaps mainly about the violence.
sentences.zh: 而且，对于斗牛爱好者来说，这不仅仅是关于暴力，甚至可能主要不是关于暴力。

sentences.en: It's about the sportsmanship, the skill, the display of expertise.
sentences.zh: 这是关于体育精神、技巧和专业展示。

sentences.en: Spectacle.
sentences.zh: 奇观。

sentences.en: Yes, and I think that that's probably true to a lot of the displays that were put on in the Coliseum.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这可能也适用于斗兽场中上演的许多表演。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's both a spectacular story, but it is quite an unsettling one, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这既是一个壮观的故事，但也是一个相当令人不安的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Just thinking about the sheer, the numbers of people who must have died.
sentences.zh: 只要想到那些必然死去的庞大数字。

sentences.en: I mean, thousands of people, I assume, over the course of its history.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想在它的历史上，有成千上万的人死去了。

sentences.en: Thousands of animals that were butchered?
sentences.zh: 成千上万的动物被屠杀？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆？

sentences.en: Butchered to make a Roman holiday, Byron put it.
sentences.zh: 正如拜伦所说，为了罗马的假日而屠杀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The scary thing is, I often think about this, if you went on holiday to Rome and they had brought back gladiatorial games,
sentences.zh: 可怕的是，我经常想，如果你去罗马度假，而他们恢复了角斗比赛，

sentences.en: how many people would go?
sentences.zh: 会有多少人去？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: How many people would go?
sentences.zh: 会有多少人去？

sentences.en: Well, we talked about this when we talked, I think, on one of our bonus episodes for our club members.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在为俱乐部成员录制的其中一期奖励节目中讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: We were asked, you know, where would you go back in time and all this sort of stuff?
sentences.zh: 有人问我们，你想回到过去哪里之类的。

sentences.en: And the question, of course, is if you went back in time to the second century AD, you know, you've gone for a long weekend,
sentences.zh: 当然，问题是如果你回到公元二世纪，你只是去度个长周末，

sentences.en: courtesy of Doctor Who or something, would you go and see the games if they were on?
sentences.zh: 借用《神秘博士》之类的手段，如果当时有比赛，你会去看吗？

sentences.en: And I think that's a really difficult one to answer because there's always a part of you that's thinking,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常难回答的问题，因为你内心总有一部分在想，

sentences.en: God, this is an extraordinary experience to see it.
sentences.zh: 天哪，能亲眼看到这真是一次非凡的体验。

sentences.en: But at the same time, the horror of it.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，那种恐怖感……

sentences.en: I mean, I wouldn't go to watch a public execution now if there were public executions in Trafalgar Square.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果现在特拉法加广场有公开处决，我绝不会去看。

sentences.en: I mean, that account by Augustine of the man going to see it, I mean, it makes it sound almost like taking heroin or something.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯丁关于那个人去看比赛的描述，听起来简直就像吸食海洛因之类的。

sentences.en: You know you shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 你知道你不该那样做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But then you take it and you're addicted.
sentences.zh: 但你还是尝试了，然后就上瘾了。

sentences.en: Well, isn't the fear, isn't the fear, the fear is not that you'll go and you'll hate it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，恐惧的不是你会去然后讨厌它。

sentences.en: The fear is that you'll go and you'll enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 恐惧的是你会去，然后你会享受它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Which is the really chilling thoughts.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正令人不寒而栗的想法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So if you want to read more about the Coliseum, you can, of course, and you should.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想了解更多关于斗兽场的信息，你当然可以，而且你应该去了解。

sentences.en: Oh, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 哦，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Go to your nearest bookshop and invest in a copy or indeed multiple copies for friends and family of Tom Holland's book, Pax.
sentences.zh: 去你最近的书店，买一本汤姆·霍兰的书《帕克斯》，或者给亲朋好友多买几本。

sentences.en: Oh, you're being so nice to me.
sentences.zh: 哦，你对我太好了。

sentences.en: Well, I'm softening you up for stuff, Tom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是在为你做铺垫，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's what it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: It's all about Rome at the height of its power and prestige.
sentences.zh: 全书讲述了罗马在权力和声望巅峰时期的故事。

sentences.en: It's about the Coliseum.
sentences.zh: 关于斗兽场。

sentences.en: It's about Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 关于庞贝。

sentences.en: It's about all these exciting things.
sentences.zh: 关于所有这些令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: The Empress, Titus and Domitian and Vespasian and so on.
sentences.zh: 皇后、提图斯、图密善、韦斯巴芗等等。

sentences.en: Great scenes.
sentences.zh: 精彩的场面。

sentences.en: And we'll be back next time, not with the Romans, but with something completely and utterly different.
sentences.zh: 我们下次再见，届时将不再谈论罗马人，而是带来完全不同的内容。

sentences.en: So we'll see you then.
sentences.zh: 那么我们到时见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
